title: The Blood of Christ
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The blood of Christ refers to His sacrificial death by which He secures forgiveness, cleansing, redemption, covenant mercy, and peace with God. His blood is precious because His life was given for sinners.
summary: The blood of Christ refers to His sacrificial death by which He secures forgiveness, cleansing, redemption, covenant mercy, and peace with God. His blood is precious because His life was given for sinners.
christFocus: Jesus shed His blood as the Lamb of God and Mediator of the new covenant. Through His blood, sinners are redeemed, cleansed, brought near, and made worshipers of God.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Scripture speaks of the blood of Christ to point to His life poured out in sacrificial death. This is not empty symbolism. Sin required a true atoning sacrifice, and Christ gave Himself.

Through His blood believers receive redemption and forgiveness. They are not bought with corruptible things, but with the precious blood of Christ, like a lamb without blemish or spot.

His blood also cleanses. The guilt and defilement of sin are answered not by denial or self-improvement, but by the blood of Jesus that cleanses from all sin.

The worship of heaven centers on the Lamb who was slain and purchased people for God by His blood. The blood of Christ will never stop being precious to the redeemed.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People often try to cleanse themselves through regret, good deeds, religious effort, or time. But guilt before God requires more than emotional relief. It requires the saving blood of Christ.

This doctrine protects the church from a bloodless Gospel. The forgiveness Christians proclaim is costly, holy, and purchased by the Savior’s sacrifice.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Do not treat the blood of Christ as common. Come to Him for cleansing, forgiveness, and peace. Worship the Lamb who was slain, and proclaim redemption as something purchased by Christ, not achieved by human effort.
